question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is** "together". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "Together" is the most suitable word for this context.
 
• The cornea and lens work jointly to focus light onto the retina.
 
• Therefore, the word "together" correctly signifies their combined effort in this process.
 
• Hence, the sentence should read: "The image is focused on the retina by the lens and cornea working together."
 
 
• The lens and cornea in our eyes work together to focus the light entering our eyes onto the retina leading to image formation which is a fundamental process in vision.
 
 

Thus, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "alone" - This implies that the lens and cornea work separately, while in reality, they work in conjunction to focus images onto the retina.
 
 
• This option isn't appropriate for this context.
 
 
 
• "consciously" - The act of seeing is not a conscious process that the eye controls on its own.
 
 
• Instead, it's an automatic, physical process controlled by the natural physiology of the eye, hence this option is not suitable.
 
 
 
• "separately" - Similar to "alone", this implies that the lens and cornea work independently of each other, which is not true as they work in unison to focus the light rays onto the retina.
